description_en: This two-storey building (known as Dyaḥ Sataḥ) is located on the western entrance of Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira (SUN0100). The middle wall of the Sataḥ is furnished with an entry door that leads towards the Bhṛṅgāreśvara temple complex. The door divides the ground floor of the building into two colonnaded spaces. The structure has seven bays demarcated by a series of columns of different sizes, and some of which have been carved. The lintel beams used in this Sataḥ were brought from Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira after it collapsed in the 1934 earthquake. The carved door head and other timber elements such as cornices have been reused as beams and floor ties. This suggests that the building was rebuilt after the 1934 earthquake.The front west bay of the Sataḥ is used for storing materials used for Pekhaḥ Jātra, the main festival of Sunāguthi, whilst the eastern bay is located within the Bhṛṅgāreśvara temple complex and is used for singingbhajanas.Sandalwood statues of Mahādeva, Gaṇeśa and Kumāra and other ritual materials used for the erection of theyaḥsipole during the Pyakhaḥ Jātra procession are stored on the upper floor. A triangular hole on the Satah's wall is worshipped as an aniconic image of Hanumān. This is located to the west of the main entrance of Bhṛṅgāreśvara Mandira,.
description_ne: भृङ्गारेश्वर मन्दिर (SUN0100) को पश्चिम प्रवेशद्वारमा रहेको यो दुईतले सतःलाई द्यः सतःको नामले चिनिन्छ । यो सतःको पछाडिको भित्तामा रहेको द्वार नै भृङ्गारेश्वर मन्दिर प्रवेश गर्ने मूल द्वार हो । सो प्रवेशद्वारको दक्षिणमा द्यः सतःको गारोमा पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी त्रिकोणाकार प्वाल बनाइएको छ । स्थानीयहरू यसलाई हनुमान् मानी पूजा गर्छन् । यस द्वारबाट भित्र छिरेपछि दायाँबायाँ पनि फल्चा रहेका देखिन्छन् जहाँ उत्तरतर्फको रेलिंग लगाइएको फल्चामा  भजन गर्ने गरिन्छ भने दक्षिणपट्टिको खुला छोडिएकोमा  मन्दिरमा आउने भक्तजनहरू आराम गर्ने गर्दछन् । फल्चाको पहिलो तलामा शिव, गणेश र कुमारका मूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् । विसं १९९० सालको भूकम्पले भृङ्गारेश्वर मन्दिर भत्केपछि मन्दिरमा रहेका काठलाई यस सतःको दलिनको रूपमा प्रयोग गरिएको देख्न सकिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: According to the Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī, King Ratna Malla established this village with 300 houses in 1513. He initiated an annual procession on the full moon day of Caitra, and it is likely that this procession was known as Pekhaḥ Jātrā back then.
